claim: Dnmt1 and Dnmt3a mRNA expression was elevated in adipose tissue, especially in epididymal and mesenteric WAT in diet-induced obesity (DIO) mouse model.
source: In a diet-induced obesity (DIO) mouse model, Dnmt1 and Dnmt3a mRNA expression was elevated in adipose tissue, especially in epididymal and mesenteric WAT (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, which present mRNA expression measurements in adipose tissue from chow- and high fat-fed mice.

claim: Dnmt3a expression was significantly induced by HFD in skeletal muscle, but to a lesser degree than in adipose tissue.
source: Dnmt3a expression was significantly induced by HFD in skeletal muscle, but to a lesser degree than in adipose tissue.
evidence: This is stated as a direct observation from the experimental data comparing tissue responses to HFD.

claim: No effect of HFD was observed on Dnmt expression in liver.
source: No effect of HFD was observed in liver (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–C showing liver Dnmt expression.

claim: In genetically obese ob/ob mice, mRNA expression of all three functional Dnmts was elevated in adipose tissue.
source: In genetically obese ob/ob mice, mRNA expression of all three functional Dnmts was elevated in adipose tissue (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B measuring Dnmt mRNA expression in ob/ob mice.

claim: Expression of Dnmts was significantly reduced after treatment with the insulin sensitizer rosiglitazone in ob/ob mice.
source: Importantly, expression of these genes was significantly reduced after treatment with the insulin sensitizer rosiglitazone (Rosi) (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B comparing Dnmt expression with and without rosiglitazone treatment.

claim: Increased adipose expression of Dnmt3a was confirmed by immunoblotting in DIO mice.
source: Increased adipose expression of Dnmt3a was confirmed by immunoblotting in DIO mice (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C and quantification in Figure 1D.

claim: Relative expression of Dnmt3a was higher in eWAT compared to skeletal muscle and liver in normal chow-fed mice.
source: Relative expression of Dnmt3a was higher in eWAT compared to skeletal muscle and liver compared in normal chow-fed mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–E comparing Dnmt3a expression across tissues.

claim: Dnmt2 and Dnmt3l mRNA displayed minimal expression in adipose tissue.
source: Dnmt2 and Dnmt3l mRNA displayed minimal expression in adipose tissue (not shown).
evidence: The authors state this as an observation from their experiments, though the data is not shown.

claim: Knock-down of individual Dnmts did not have a major impact on the basal level of insulin sensitivity when assessed by insulin-stimulated glucose uptake.
source: Knock-down of individual Dnmts did not have a major impact on the basal level of insulin sensitivity when assessed by insulin-stimulated glucose uptake (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–E.

claim: Knock-down of Dnmt3a, but not Dnmt1 or Dnmt3b, protected adipocytes from Dex- and TNF-mediated IR as assessed by insulin-stimulated glucose uptake and signal transduction.
source: However, knock-down of Dnmt3a, but not Dnmt1 or Dnmt3b, protected adipocytes from Dex- and TNF-mediated IR as assessed by insulin-stimulated glucose uptake and signal transduction (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data and Western blot data shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–E.

claim: Overexpression of Dnmt3a and 3b, but not Dnmt1, potently inhibited insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in mature 3T3-L1 adipocytes.
source: Interestingly, overexpression of Dnmt3a and 3b, but not Dnmt1, potently inhibited insulin-stimulated glucose uptake (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Overexpression of Dnmt3a powerfully inhibited insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in in vitro differentiated adipocytes from human adipose derived stem cells.
source: Additionally, we tested whether the causal role of Dnmt3a in the development of insulin resistance is conserved in human adipocytes. Overexpression of Dnmt3a powerfully inhibited insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in in vitro differentiated adipocytes from human adipose derived stem cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data in human adipocytes shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Dnmt3a is both necessary and sufficient to mediate IR in adipocytes in a cell autonomous manner.
source: Together, our gain- and loss-of-function studies in vitro show that Dnmt3a is both necessary and sufficient to mediate IR in adipocytes in a cell autonomous manner.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the gain- and loss-of-function experimental data presented in the preceding paragraphs and figures.

claim: Both 5-azacytidine and RG-108 Dnmt inhibitors blocked Dex- and TNF-mediated IR.
source: Remarkably, both Dnmt inhibitors blocked Dex- and TNF-mediated IR (Figure 3A,B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data shown in Figure 3A,B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The naturally occurring Dnmt inhibitors epigallocatechin gallate (ECCG) and theaflavin-3,3′-digallate (TF-3) showed insulin-sensitizing activity in the setting of Dex- and TNF-mediated IR.
source: In addition to these synthetic inhibitors, the naturally occurring Dnmt inhibitors (Rajavelu et al., 2011) epigallocatechin gallate (ECCG) and theaflavin-3,3′-digallate (TF-3) also showed insulin-sensitizing activity in the setting of Dex- and TNF-mediated IR (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–F and cites prior work on these compounds as Dnmt inhibitors.

claim: Unlike the wild-type allele, Dnmt3a C706S was unable to suppress insulin-stimulated glucose uptake.
source: To further probe this hypothesis, we overexpressed a catalytically inactive allele of Dnmt3a (C706S) (Hsieh, 1999). Unlike the wild-type allele, Dnmt3a C706S was unable to suppress insulin-stimulated glucose uptake (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data shown in Figure 3C comparing wild-type and catalytically inactive Dnmt3a, and cites prior work characterizing the C706S mutation.

claim: DNA methyltransferase activity is essential for Dnmt3a to mediate IR.
source: Together, the pharmacological and genetic evidence indicates that DNA methyltransferase activity is essential for Dnmt3a to mediate IR.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the pharmacological inhibitor experiments and the catalytically inactive mutant experiment.

claim: On chow diet, male WT and Dnmt3aAdiKO animals did not show any obvious change in their body weight, insulin sensitivity, glucose tolerance, or insulin levels.
source: On chow diet, male WT and Dnmt3aAdiKO animals did not show any obvious change in their body weight, insulin sensitivity, glucose tolerance, or insulin levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–D measuring these metabolic parameters in chow-fed mice.

claim: On HFD (45% fat), Dnmt3aAdiKO mice showed no significant differences in body weight or composition relative to littermate controls.
source: On HFD (45% fat), Dnmt3aAdiKO mice still showed no significant differences in body weight or composition relative to littermate controls (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by body weight and body composition data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The effect of long-term fasting (16 hr) on body weight or body composition did not differ between genotypes.
source: Moreover, the effect of long-term fasting (16 hr) on body weight or body composition did not differ between genotypes (Figure 4C), suggesting that gross energy homeostasis is not altered in the knock-out animals.
evidence: The claim is supported by fasting data shown in Figure 4C and includes an inference about energy homeostasis.

claim: High fat fed male Dnmt3aAdiKO mice exhibited improved glucose tolerance.
source: Despite no obvious change in energy balance, high fat fed male Dnmt3aAdiKO mice exhibited improved glucose tolerance (Figure 4D,E)
evidence: The claim is supported by glucose tolerance test data shown in Figure 4D,E.

claim: High fat fed male Dnmt3aAdiKO mice exhibited improved insulin sensitivity.
source: high fat fed male Dnmt3aAdiKO mice exhibited improved glucose tolerance (Figure 4D,E) and insulin sensitivity (Figure 4F,G)
evidence: The claim is supported by insulin tolerance test data shown in Figure 4F,G.

claim: High fat fed male Dnmt3aAdiKO mice had reduced serum insulin in the fed state.
source: high fat fed male Dnmt3aAdiKO mice exhibited improved glucose tolerance (Figure 4D,E) and insulin sensitivity (Figure 4F,G) with reduced serum insulin in the fed state (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by serum insulin measurements shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Male Dnmt3aAdiKO mice display increased insulin signal transduction in adipose tissue, as demonstrated by increased insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of IRS and AKT.
source: Consistent with their metabolic improvement, male Dnmt3aAdiKO mice display increased insulin signal transduction in adipose tissue, as demonstrated by increased insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of IRS and AKT (Figure 4I,J).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4I,J.

claim: Female Dnmt3aAdiKO mice display improved insulin sensitivity and glucose tolerance on HFD without a change in body weight.
source: Similarly, female Dnmt3aAdiKO mice display improved insulin sensitivity and glucose tolerance on HFD without a change in body weight (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–C.

claim: No consistent change in the expression of major thermogenic genes such as Ucp1 and Ppargc1a was found in either iWAT and BAT of Dnmt3aAdiKO mice.
source: With regard to the former, we found no consistent change in the expression of major thermogenic genes such as Ucp1 and Ppargc1a in either iWAT and BAT (Figure 4—figure supplement 4A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4A,B.

claim: Gene expression analysis showed a nonsignificant trend toward reduced expression of proinflammatory genes such as Tnfa and Ccl2 in the eWAT of Dnmt3aAdiKO mice.
source: Additionally, gene expression analysis showed a nonsignificant trend toward reduced expression of proinflammatory genes such as Tnfa and Ccl2 (which encodes MCP-1) in the eWAT of Dnmt3aAdiKO mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5A.

claim: No obvious change in the density of crown-like structures was observed between WT and KO tissues.
source: We also saw no obvious change in the density of crown-like structures between WT and KO tissues (Figure 4—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5B.

claim: Adipose-specific deletion of Dnmt3a confers protection from diet-induced IR in a manner that is independent of adiposity, inflammation, or browning of white adipose tissue.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that adipose-specific deletion of Dnmt3a confers protection from diet-induced IR in a manner that is independent of adiposity, inflammation, or browning of white adipose tissue.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the multiple lines of experimental data showing improved insulin sensitivity without changes in body weight, inflammation markers, or thermogenic gene expression.

claim: 97 genes were repressed after shRNA-mediated Dnmt3a knock-down.
source: We found that 97 genes were repressed after shRNA-mediated Dnmt3a knock-down, while only eight genes were up-regulated in the presence of excess Dnmt3a; the single gene showing concordant regulation was Dnmt3a itself (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Only eight genes were up-regulated in the presence of excess Dnmt3a.
source: We found that 97 genes were repressed after shRNA-mediated Dnmt3a knock-down, while only eight genes were up-regulated in the presence of excess Dnmt3a; the single gene showing concordant regulation was Dnmt3a itself (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The single gene showing concordant regulation in both Dnmt3a knockdown and overexpression was Dnmt3a itself.
source: We found that 97 genes were repressed after shRNA-mediated Dnmt3a knock-down, while only eight genes were up-regulated in the presence of excess Dnmt3a; the single gene showing concordant regulation was Dnmt3a itself (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: 290 genes were induced by Dnmt3a knock-down.
source: Conversely, 290 genes were induced by Dnmt3a knock-down, and 36 genes showed diminished expression after Dnmt3a overexpression; seven genes were concordantly regulated by both manipulations (Figure 5B and C and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: 36 genes showed diminished expression after Dnmt3a overexpression.
source: Conversely, 290 genes were induced by Dnmt3a knock-down, and 36 genes showed diminished expression after Dnmt3a overexpression; seven genes were concordantly regulated by both manipulations (Figure 5B and C and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: Seven genes were concordantly regulated by both Dnmt3a knockdown and overexpression as negative targets.
source: Conversely, 290 genes were induced by Dnmt3a knock-down, and 36 genes showed diminished expression after Dnmt3a overexpression; seven genes were concordantly regulated by both manipulations (Figure 5B and C and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: Dnmt3a works primarily as a repressor of gene expression.
source: These data are consistent with the expectation that Dnmt3a works primarily as a repressor of gene expression.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the RNA-seq data showing more genes induced by knockdown than repressed by overexpression.

claim: Fgf21 is a negative target gene of Dnmt3a.
source: Among the concordantly-regulated negative target genes of Dnmt3a, we were immediately struck by the presence of Fgf21.
evidence: This is stated based on the RNA-seq analysis identifying Fgf21 among the concordantly regulated genes.

claim: FGF21 is known to facilitate glucose uptake in adipocytes.
source: FGF21 is known to facilitate glucose uptake in adipocytes (Ge et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2014; Minard et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim cites three prior studies demonstrating FGF21's role in glucose uptake.

claim: FGF21 is a positive target gene of PPARγ.
source: FGF21 is known to facilitate glucose uptake in adipocytes (Ge et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2014; Minard et al., 2016), and is a positive target gene of PPARγ (Muise et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim cites a prior study showing PPARγ regulation of FGF21.

claim: Mice lacking FGF21 do not support Rosi-mediated insulin sensitization in vivo.
source: Furthermore, mice lacking FGF21 do not support Rosi-mediated insulin sensitization in vivo (Dutchak et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim cites a prior study demonstrating the requirement of FGF21 for rosiglitazone's insulin-sensitizing effects.

claim: Fgf21 expression is reduced in cultured adipocytes overexpressing Dnmt3a.
source: We confirmed by Q-PCR that Fgf21 expression is indeed reduced in cultured adipocytes overexpressing Dnmt3a, is increased in cells expressing shDnmt3a, and most importantly, is up-regulated in the adipose tissue of Dnmt3aAdiKO mice (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Fgf21 expression is increased in cells expressing shDnmt3a.
source: We confirmed by Q-PCR that Fgf21 expression is indeed reduced in cultured adipocytes overexpressing Dnmt3a, is increased in cells expressing shDnmt3a, and most importantly, is up-regulated in the adipose tissue of Dnmt3aAdiKO mice (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Fgf21 expression is up-regulated in the adipose tissue of Dnmt3aAdiKO mice.
source: We confirmed by Q-PCR that Fgf21 expression is indeed reduced in cultured adipocytes overexpressing Dnmt3a, is increased in cells expressing shDnmt3a, and most importantly, is up-regulated in the adipose tissue of Dnmt3aAdiKO mice (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Serum levels of Fgf21 were reduced in HFD-fed Dnmt3aAdiKO mice compared to controls.
source: Unlike adipose tissue levels, serum levels of Fgf21 were reduced in HFD-fed Dnmt3aAdiKO mice compared to controls (Figure 5—figure supplement 5–).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA measurements shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: Recombinant FGF21 restored insulin sensitivity in 3T3-L1 adipocytes that overexpress Dnmt3a in a dose-dependent manner.
source: To determine whether restoration of FGF21 levels could ameliorate Dnmt3a-mediated IR, we treated 3T3-L1 adipocytes that overexpress Dnmt3a with recombinant FGF21, which restored insulin sensitivity in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The level of DNA methylation at gene promoters is inversely correlated with mRNA expression.
source: In general, the level of DNA methylation at gene promoters is inversely correlated with mRNA expression (Jones, 2012).
evidence: This claim cites a prior review establishing the general relationship between DNA methylation and gene expression.

claim: Genomic DNA hypermethylation at Fgf21 promoter regions was detected in Dnmt3a overexpressor 3T3-L1 cells compared to controls.
source: Using methylated DNA precipitation PCR (MeDIP-qPCR), we detected genomic DNA hypermethylation at Fgf21 promoter regions in Dnmt3a overexpressor 3T3-L1 cells compared to controls (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by MeDIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: DNA hypomethylation of Fgf21 promoter regions was seen in Dnmt3a knock-down cells.
source: Conversely, DNA hypomethylation of these same regions was seen in Dnmt3a knock-down cells (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by MeDIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Reduced DNA methylation at the Fgf21 promoter was found in fractionated adipocytes of Dnmt3aAdiKO animals.
source: In addition to the in vitro models, we conducted MeDIP-qPCR analysis using genomic DNA from fractionated adipocytes of Dnmt3aAdiKO and control animals, finding reduced DNA methylation at the Fgf21 promoter in KO cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by MeDIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Co-transfection of Dnmt3a potently inhibited promoter activity of Fgf21.
source: Consistent with DNA methylation pattern at the Fgf21 promoter region, co-transfection of Dnmt3a potently inhibited promoter activity of Fgf21 (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Dnmt3a-mediated suppression of Fgf21 involves changes in DNA methylation profile at key promoter regions.
source: Together, these data suggest that Dnmt3a-mediated suppression of Fgf21 involves changes in DNA methylation profile at key promoter regions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the MeDIP-qPCR and reporter assay data.

claim: Hypermethylation of four CpG sites annotated to FGF21 was found in adipose tissue of subjects with type 2 diabetes compared with non-diabetic controls.
source: In line with our mouse data, we found hypermethylation of four CpG sites annotated to FGF21 in adipose tissue of subjects with type 2 diabetes compared with non-diabetic controls (Figure 7A and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA methylation data from human adipose tissue shown in Figure 7A.

claim: A negative correlation was found between DNA methylation and mRNA expression of FGF21 in human adipose tissue.
source: Further, we found a negative correlation between DNA methylation and mRNA expression of FGF21 in human adipose tissue (Figure 7B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 7B–E.

claim: Increased DNA methylation of FGF21 plays a role in the regulation of adipose FGF21 expression in association with metabolic disease.
source: Together, these data support a role for increased DNA methylation of FGF21 in the regulation of adipose FGF21 expression in association with metabolic disease.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the human adipose tissue DNA methylation and expression data.

claim: Genetic differences cannot fully explain many features of obesity and T2D, such as discordance in monozygotic twins, and the close relationship with lifestyle factors.
source: While genetics plays an important role in obesity and T2D, genetic differences cannot fully explain many features of these conditions, such as discordance in monozygotic twins, and the close relationship with lifestyle factors (McCarthy, 2010; Morris et al., 2012; Voight et al., 2010; Zeggini et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim cites four prior studies discussing the limitations of genetic explanations for obesity and T2D.

claim: The vast majority of GWAS-proven allelic variants associated with T2D correspond much better to altered insulin secretion and islet function rather than to IR per se.
source: Of note, the vast majority of GWAS-proven allelic variants associated with T2D correspond much better to altered insulin secretion and islet function rather than to IR per se (Voight et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim cites a prior GWAS study characterizing T2D-associated genetic variants.

claim: A recent epigenome-wide association study (EWAS) linked alterations in DNA methylation to whole-body insulin sensitivity.
source: This notion has been borne out by a recent epigenome-wide association study (EWAS) linking alterations in DNA methylation to whole-body insulin sensitivity (Zhao et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim cites a prior EWAS study linking DNA methylation to insulin sensitivity.

claim: Genetic variants may cause disease in a DNA methylation-dependent manner, as has recently been shown for T2D and obesity.
source: Importantly, even genetic variants may cause disease in a DNA methylation-dependent manner, as has recently been shown for T2D and obesity (Dayeh et al., 2013; Elliott et al., 2017; Nilsson et al., 2014; Olsson et al., 2014; Volkov et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim cites five prior studies demonstrating DNA methylation-dependent effects of genetic variants in metabolic disease.

claim: Adipose tissue from patients with T2D exhibit numerous methylation and expression differences relative to unrelated healthy controls, with many of the same changes also seen in twin pairs discordant for T2D.
source: We have also shown that adipose tissue from patients with T2D exhibit numerous methylation and expression differences relative to unrelated healthy controls, with many of the same changes also seen in twin pairs discordant for T2D (Nilsson et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim cites a prior study by the authors showing DNA methylation differences in T2D adipose tissue.

claim: Administration of pan-inhibitors of histone deacetylase exerts beneficial metabolic effects in both mice and humans, such as increased energy expenditure, insulin sensitivity and secretion.
source: For example, administration of pan-inhibitors of histone deacetylase exerts beneficial metabolic effects in both mice and humans, such as increased energy expenditure, insulin sensitivity and secretion (Christensen et al., 2011; Daneshpajooh et al., 2017; Sharma and Taliyan, 2016; Ye, 2013).
evidence: This claim cites four prior studies demonstrating metabolic effects of HDAC inhibitors.

claim: DNA methyltransferase inhibitors have been shown to have an insulin-sensitizing effect in vivo and in vitro.
source: DNA methyltransferase inhibitors have also been shown to have an insulin-sensitizing effect in vivo and in vitro (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim cites a prior study demonstrating insulin-sensitizing effects of DNMT inhibitors.

claim: Mutant mouse models carrying loss-of function histone modifiers (e.g. Mll2, Ehmt1, Jmhd2a Lsd1) were shown to have profound impact on whole body metabolism.
source: In line with pharmacological studies, mutant mouse models carrying loss-of function histone modifiers (e.g. Mll2, Ehmt1, Jmhd2a Lsd1) were shown to have profound impact on whole body metabolism (Lee et al., 2006; Ohno et al., 2013; Sambeat et al., 2016; Tateishi et al., 2009; Zeng et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim cites five prior studies demonstrating metabolic effects of histone modifier mutations.

claim: Metabolic consequences in mouse models carrying mutations of histone modifiers appear to be mainly attributable to changes in body weight.
source: It should be noted that metabolic consequences in mouse models carrying mutations of histone modifiers appear to be mainly attributable to changes in body weight.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies on histone modifier mutant mice.

claim: Adipose-specific Dnmt3a KO mice are relatively unique in that they display improved insulin sensitivity without a change in adiposity or body weight.
source: Unlike these examples, adipose-specific Dnmt3a KO mice are relatively unique in that they display improved insulin sensitivity without a change in adiposity or body weight.
evidence: This is a summary statement comparing the current findings to prior studies, drawing on the experimental data presented earlier.

claim: The effect of adipose-specific Dnmt3a deletion on insulin action is not dependent on increased beige or brown adipocytes, or on reducing intra-adipose inflammation.
source: Similarly, the effect on insulin action is not dependent on increased beige or brown adipocytes, or on reducing intra-adipose inflammation.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data showing no changes in thermogenic genes or inflammation markers.

claim: Overexpression of Dnmt3a is sufficient to induce cell autonomous IR in vitro.
source: Our in vitro study indicates that overexpression of Dnmt3a is sufficient to induce cell autonomous IR, however, it does not seem to be the case in vivo.
evidence: This is a summary of the in vitro findings from earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Transgenic expression of Dnmt3a per se was not sufficient to render whole body IR and glucose intolerance on chow, HFD, or high methyl diet with chow diet.
source: Kamei et al showed that transgenic expression of Dnmt3a per se was not sufficient to render whole body IR and glucose intolerance (Kamei et al., 2010) on chow, HFD, or high methyl diet with chow diet.
evidence: This claim cites a prior study by Kamei et al. on Dnmt3a transgenic mice.

claim: Kamei et al. observed only a mild increase in the gene expression of proinflammatory cytokines (i.e. Mcp1 and Tnfa) when animals were put on HFD.
source: Authors observed only a mild increase in the gene expression of proinflammatory cytokines (i.e. Mcp1 and Tnfa) when animals were put on HFD.
evidence: This claim describes findings from the Kamei et al. study.

claim: The major caveat of the Kamei et al. study is the use of aP2 promoter to drive the transgene expression.
source: It should be noted that the major caveat of this study is the use of aP2 promoter to drive the transgene expression (Jeffery et al., 2014; Kang et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim cites three prior studies discussing issues with the aP2 promoter.

claim: Fgf21 is better known as a hepatokine, and the liver is the main source of circulating Fgf21.
source: Fgf21 is better known as a hepatokine, and the liver is the main source of circulating Fgf21 (Markan et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim cites a prior study characterizing Fgf21 as a hepatokine.

claim: Adipose Fgf21 probably does not circulate, but rather acts in an autocrine/paracrine manner.
source: Adipose Fgf21 probably does not circulate, but rather acts in an autocrine/paracrine manner (Dutchak et al., 2012; Markan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim cites two prior studies suggesting autocrine/paracrine action of adipose Fgf21.

claim: Studies have shown a positive correlation between insulin and circulating Fgf21 levels.
source: Studies have shown a positive correlation between insulin and circulating Fgf21 levels (Chavez et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim cites three prior studies showing correlation between insulin and Fgf21.

claim: Insulin may be a key determinant of Fgf21 in serum.
source: Studies have shown a positive correlation between insulin and circulating Fgf21 levels (Chavez et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2008), suggesting that insulin may be a key determinant of Fgf21 in serum.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies showing correlation between insulin and Fgf21.

claim: The reduced insulin levels in Dnmt3a KO mice on HFD may have led to reduction of Fgf21 production in liver.
source: Thus, it is possible that the reduced insulin levels in Dnmt3a KO mice on HFD may have led to reduction of Fgf21 production in liver.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed reduced insulin and serum Fgf21 levels in the KO mice.

claim: Fgf21 serum levels are often elevated in obesity-associated IR, possibly reflecting resistance to Fgf21.
source: This notion is in line with the finding that Fgf21 serum levels are often elevated in obesity-associated IR (Fisher and Maratos-Flier, 2016; Morrice et al., 2017), possibly reflecting resistance to Fgf21 (Fisher et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim cites three prior studies on Fgf21 levels in obesity and potential Fgf21 resistance.

claim: The local activity of Fgf21 within the fat pad is important for the improved insulin sensitivity in the knock-out mice.
source: We propose that the local activity of Fgf21 within the fat pad is important for the improved insulin sensitivity in the knock-out mice, although formal proof of this idea would require generating adipose tissue-specific Dnmt3a and Fgf21 double knockout mice.
evidence: This is a proposed hypothesis based on the experimental findings, with acknowledgment that formal proof requires additional experiments.

claim: Three independent studies demonstrated that mutant mice devoid of Fgf21 signaling in adipose tissue secondary to ablation of FGFR1 or bKlotho, were refractory to the insulin-sensitizing effect of Fgf21 administration.
source: For example, three independent studies demonstrated that mutant mice devoid of Fgf21 signaling in adipose tissue secondary to ablation of FGFR1 or bKlotho, were refractory to the insulin-sensitizing effect of Fgf21 administration (Adams et al., 2013; BonDurant et al., 2017; Ding et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim cites three prior studies demonstrating the requirement of adipose Fgf21 signaling for insulin sensitization.

claim: Some studies suggested that adiponectin is an essential mediator of Fgf21 metabolic action.
source: Some of these studies (Adams et al., 2013; Ding et al., 2012) suggested that adiponectin is an essential mediator of Fgf21 metabolic action
evidence: This claim cites two prior studies suggesting adiponectin mediates Fgf21 action.

claim: One study suggested that adiponectin is dispensable for Fgf21 metabolic action.
source: the other study (BonDurant et al., 2017) suggested that adiponectin is dispensable.
evidence: This claim cites a prior study suggesting adiponectin is not required for Fgf21 action.

claim: There was a trend toward increased mRNA expression of Adipoq in both L1 and primary Dnmt3a KO adipocytes, albeit it did not reach statistical significance.
source: In our studies, albeit it did not reach statistical significance, there was a trend toward increased mRNA expression of Adipoq in both L1 and primary Dnmt3a KO adipocytes (not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the authors' experiments, though the data is not shown.

claim: Control of Fgf21 expression appears to be highly tissue-specific.
source: Control of Fgf21 expression appears to be highly tissue-specific.
evidence: This is a general statement introducing the tissue-specific regulation of Fgf21.

claim: PPARγ is an important driver of Fgf21 in adipose tissue, while PPARα serves that role in liver.
source: For example, PPARγ is an important driver of Fgf21 in adipose tissue, while PPARα serves that role in liver (Dutchak et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim cites a prior study characterizing tissue-specific regulation of Fgf21.

claim: Other studies have demonstrated that Fgf21 is positively regulated by PPARγ in fat.
source: Other studies have also demonstrated that Fgf21 is positively regulated by PPARγ in fat (Muise et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim cites two prior studies showing PPARγ regulation of Fgf21 in adipose tissue.

claim: Global DNA methylation profiling will be necessary to identify differentially methylated regions in the setting of Dnmt3a gain- and loss-of function.
source: In addition to focused studies on Fgf21 promoter regions, global DNA methylation profiling will be necessary to identify differentially methylated regions in the setting of Dnmt3a gain- and loss-of function.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions needed to fully characterize Dnmt3a's effects.

claim: A recent study demonstrated that Dnmt1 may contribute to obesity-associated inflammation and insulin resistance by promoting hypermethylation at the Adipoq locus.
source: A recent study demonstrated that Dnmt1 may contribute to obesity-associated inflammation and insulin resistance by promoting hypermethylation at the Adipoq locus (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim cites a prior study on Dnmt1's role in insulin resistance.

claim: Elevated Dnmt1 levels were observed in the adipose tissue of obese animals.
source: Concordant with this study, we also see elevated Dnmt1 levels in the adipose tissue of obese animals.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the authors' experiments shown earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Knockdown of Dnmt1 did not rescue insulin sensitivity in the setting of Dex or TNF.
source: However, knockdown of Dnmt1 did not rescue insulin sensitivity in the setting of Dex or TNF, and overexpression of Dnmt1 did not reduce insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in cultured adipocytes.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the authors' experiments shown earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Overexpression of Dnmt1 did not reduce insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in cultured adipocytes.
source: However, knockdown of Dnmt1 did not rescue insulin sensitivity in the setting of Dex or TNF, and overexpression of Dnmt1 did not reduce insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in cultured adipocytes.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the authors' experiments shown earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Adipose-specific deletion of Dnmt3a promoted insulin sensitivity even in weight-matched obese animals.
source: Based on those criteria, we chose to focus on Dnmt3a, and showed that adipose-specific deletion of this gene promoted insulin sensitivity even in weight-matched obese animals.
evidence: This is a summary of the in vivo findings from earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Adipoq was not identified as a regulated target after either deletion or overexpression of Dnmt3a.
source: Of note, we did not identify Adipoq as a regulated target after either deletion or overexpression of Dnmt3a.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Dnmt3a is not induced by lipids (e.g. palmitate), pro-inflammatory signals (e.g. IL-6, LPS), high doses of insulin, or high glucose in cultured adipocytes.
source: Despite some effort, we have not yet identified the mechanism by which Dnmt3a expression is increased in obesity. We found that Dnmt3a is not induced by lipids (e.g. palmitate), pro-inflammatory signals (e.g. IL-6, LPS), high doses of insulin, or high glucose in cultured adipocytes (not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the authors' experiments, though the data is not shown.

claim: In vivo administration of thiazolidinediones normalized the expression of Dnmt3a in ob/ob mice but not in lean control animals.
source: In our study, in vivo administration of thiazolidinediones normalized the expression of Dnmt3a in ob/ob mice but not in lean control animals.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the authors' experiments shown earlier in the manuscript.

claim: The mechanism by which PPARγ represses gene expression is not entirely clear.
source: The mechanism by which PPARγ represses gene expression is not entirely clear.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Trans-repression through binding of inflammatory transcription factors like NF-κB and AP-1 has been proposed as a general mechanism for PPARγ-mediated gene repression.
source: Trans-repression through binding of inflammatory transcription factors like NF-κB and AP-1 has been proposed as a general mechanism for this type of effect (Glass and Saijo, 2010)
evidence: This claim cites a prior study proposing a mechanism for PPARγ-mediated repression.

claim: There are PPARγ binding sites near the Dnmt3a TSS.
source: although we note that there are PPARγ binding sites near the Dnmt3a TSS (not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the authors' analysis, though the data is not shown.

claim: It is unclear if direct or indirect (i.e. trans-repression) mechanisms account for the actions of rosiglitazone on Dnmt3a expression in obesity.
source: It is thus unclear if direct or indirect (i.e. trans-repression) mechanisms account for the actions of rosiglitazone on Dnmt3a expression in obesity.
evidence: This is a statement acknowledging uncertainty about the mechanism.

claim: Dnmt3a is a novel epigenetic mediator of adipose IR in vitro and in vivo.
source: In summary, we have identified a novel role for Dnmt3a as an epigenetic mediator of adipose IR in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is the main conclusion summarizing all the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Future studies will be required to fully elucidate the full range of Dnmt3a's target genomic regions and metabolic effects.
source: Future studies will be required to fully elucidate the full range of its target genomic regions and metabolic effects.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Insulin resistance is generally defined as a reduced ability of insulin to provoke metabolic responses, such as glucose uptake.
source: Insulin resistance (IR) is generally defined as a reduced ability of insulin to provoke metabolic responses, such as glucose uptake.
evidence: This is a standard definition from the field.

claim: Several mechanistic drivers of IR have been proposed, including defects in the insulin signal transduction pathway, dysfunctional mitochondrial respiration, and ER stress.
source: Several mechanistic drivers of IR have been proposed, including defects in the insulin signal transduction pathway, dysfunctional mitochondrial respiration, and ER stress (Boucher et al., 2014; Gregor and Hotamisligil, 2011; Houstis et al., 2006; Ozcan et al., 2004; Samuel and Shulman, 2012).
evidence: This claim cites five prior studies proposing various mechanisms of insulin resistance.

claim: Nuclear pathways (i.e. transcriptional and epigenomic mechanisms) are likely to play an important role in IR development, given that IR often develops over a time course that is inconsistent with rapid signal transduction events.
source: Nuclear pathways in particular (i.e. transcriptional and epigenomic mechanisms) are likely to play an important role, given that IR often develops over a time course that is inconsistent with rapid signal transduction events (Kang et al., 2015; Tan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim cites two prior studies and makes an inference about the role of nuclear pathways based on the time course of IR development.

claim: There is a large body of data from humans and rodents indicating that the propensity for IR can be passed transgenerationally.
source: Furthermore, there is a large body of data from humans and rodents indicating that the propensity for IR can be passed transgenerationally; such 'fetal programming' studies strongly imply an epigenetic basis for IR (Carone et al., 2010; Heijmans et al., 2008; Li et al., 2010; Tobi et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim cites four prior studies on transgenerational transmission of IR propensity.

claim: Fetal programming studies strongly imply an epigenetic basis for IR.
source: Furthermore, there is a large body of data from humans and rodents indicating that the propensity for IR can be passed transgenerationally; such 'fetal programming' studies strongly imply an epigenetic basis for IR (Carone et al., 2010; Heijmans et al., 2008; Li et al., 2010; Tobi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited fetal programming studies.

claim: Thiazolidinedione drugs, which activate the transcription factor PPARγ, provide one of the only pharmacological therapies for IR.
source: Finally, thiazolidinedione drugs, which activate the transcription factor PPARγ, provide one of the only pharmacological therapies for IR (Soccio et al., 2014; Step et al., 2014; Sugii et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim cites three prior studies on thiazolidinediones as IR therapy.

claim: Epigenomic and transcriptional mechanisms must be in play in the etiopathogenesis of IR.
source: Taken together, these data strongly suggest that epigenomic and transcriptional mechanisms must be in play in the etiopathogenesis of IR (Kang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the various lines of evidence presented and cites a prior review.

claim: DNA methylation is a reversible epigenetic mark involving the covalent transfer of a methyl group to the C-5 position of a cytosine residue, usually in the context of a CpG doublet, by DNA methyltransferases (Dnmts).
source: DNA methylation is a reversible epigenetic mark involving the covalent transfer of a methyl group to the C-5 position of a cytosine residue, usually in the context of a CpG doublet, by DNA methyltransferases (Dnmts) (Robertson, 2005).
evidence: This is a standard definition from the field, citing a prior review.

claim: Emerging evidence suggests that methylated DNA undergoes dynamic and reversible remodeling in somatic cells during developmental, physiological, and pathogenic pathophysiological processes.
source: Long thought to be a static epigenetic mark, emerging evidence suggests that methylated DNA undergoes dynamic and reversible remodeling in somatic cells during developmental, physiological, and pathogenic pathophysiological processes (Barres et al., 2013; 2009; Benner et al., 2015; Kirchner et al., 2016; Multhaup et al., 2015; Siersbæk et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim cites six prior studies demonstrating dynamic DNA methylation changes.

claim: A bout of intense exercise can induce DNA hypomethylation at the PPARGC1a locus in human skeletal muscle within hours, followed by increased gene expression; these effects were reversed after resting.
source: As an example, a bout of intense exercise can induce DNA hypomethylation at the PPARGC1a locus in human skeletal muscle within hours, followed by increased gene expression; these effects were reversed after resting (Barrès et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim cites a prior study demonstrating rapid, reversible DNA methylation changes with exercise.

claim: The obesity-prone agouti mouse has reduced DNA methylation at the regulatory region for the Agouti gene, leading to enhanced expression and subsequent inhibition of the satiety-inducing MC4 receptor.
source: For example, the obesity-prone agouti mouse has reduced DNA methylation at the regulatory region for the Agouti gene, leading to enhanced expression and subsequent inhibition of the satiety-inducing MC4 receptor (Xie et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim cites a prior study on DNA methylation in the agouti mouse model.

claim: Multiple studies have shown that changes in DNA methylation at key metabolic genes, such as Cox7a1, IGF-2, and Pomc, associate with various metabolic insults including aging, obesity, anorexia, and prenatal exposure to famine.
source: Multiple studies have shown that changes in DNA methylation at key metabolic genes, such as Cox7a1 (Rönn et al., 2008), IGF-2 (Heijmans et al., 2008), and Pomc (Ehrlich et al., 2010), associate with various metabolic insults including aging, obesity, anorexia, and prenatal exposure to famine.
evidence: This claim cites three prior studies linking DNA methylation changes to metabolic conditions.

claim: Recent genome-wide profiling studies have identified distinct global DNA methylation patterns that associate with obesity and diabetes in humans.
source: Moreover, recent genome-wide profiling studies have identified distinct global DNA methylation patterns that associate with obesity and diabetes in humans (Dayeh et al., 2014; Feinberg et al., 2010; Kirchner et al., 2016; Multhaup et al., 2015; Nilsson et al., 2015; Volkmar et al., 2012; Volkov et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim cites seven prior genome-wide studies linking DNA methylation to metabolic disease.

claim: Altered DNA methylation is linked to the transgenerational passage of metabolic disorders.
source: Altered DNA methylation is linked to the transgenerational passage of metabolic disorders (Ng et al., 2010; Wei et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim cites two prior studies linking DNA methylation to transgenerational metabolic effects.

claim: The cause-and-effect relationship between DNA methylation and metabolic dysregulation remains largely unknown.
source: Despite numerous studies showing a link between DNA methylation and metabolic dysregulation, the cause-and-effect relationship between the two remains largely unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: In mammals, five Dnmt family members have been identified: Dnmt1, Dnmt2 (also known as Trdmt1), Dnmt3a, Dnmt3b and Dnmt3l.
source: In mammals, five Dnmt family members have been identified: Dnmt1, Dnmt2 (also known as Trdmt1), Dnmt3a, Dnmt3b and Dnmt3l, yet only three (Dnmt1, 3a, and 3b) possess DNA methyltransferase activity (Robertson, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the field, citing a prior review.

claim: Only three Dnmts (Dnmt1, 3a, and 3b) possess DNA methyltransferase activity.
source: In mammals, five Dnmt family members have been identified: Dnmt1, Dnmt2 (also known as Trdmt1), Dnmt3a, Dnmt3b and Dnmt3l, yet only three (Dnmt1, 3a, and 3b) possess DNA methyltransferase activity (Robertson, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the field, citing a prior review.

claim: Dnmt1 (the maintenance DNA methyltransferase) has a preference to methylate hemimethylated DNA whereas Dnmt3a and 3b prefer unmethylated DNA as substrate, and thus act as de novo DNA methyltransferases.
source: Dnmt1 (the maintenance DNA methyltransferase) has a preference to methylate hemimethylated DNA whereas Dnmt3a and 3b prefer unmethylated DNA as substrate, and thus act as de novo DNA methyltransferases (Robertson, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the field, citing a prior review.

claim: Dnmt3l is homologous to the other Dnmt3s but lacks catalytic activity.
source: Dnmt3l is homologous to the other Dnmt3s but lacks catalytic activity (Robertson, 2005)
evidence: This is established knowledge from the field, citing a prior review.

claim: Dnmt2 has sequence homology to all Dnmts but methylates cytoplasmic tRNA, and not DNA.
source: Dnmt2 has sequence homology to all Dnmts but methylates cytoplasmic tRNA, and not DNA (Robertson, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the field, citing a prior review.

claim: Administration of a small molecule Dnmt inhibitor has been shown to improve insulin sensitivity in the setting of obesity, in part by demethylating the Adipoq promoter.
source: Administration of a small molecule Dnmt inhibitor has been shown to improve insulin sensitivity in the setting of obesity, in part by demethylating the Adipoq promoter, and a role for Dnmt1 in this process was suggested by genetic knockdown studies in cultured adipocytes (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim cites a prior study demonstrating insulin-sensitizing effects of Dnmt inhibitors.

claim: A role for Dnmt1 in obesity-associated insulin resistance was suggested by genetic knockdown studies in cultured adipocytes.
source: Administration of a small molecule Dnmt inhibitor has been shown to improve insulin sensitivity in the setting of obesity, in part by demethylating the Adipoq promoter, and a role for Dnmt1 in this process was suggested by genetic knockdown studies in cultured adipocytes (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim cites a prior study suggesting Dnmt1's role based on knockdown experiments.

claim: Dnmt3a plays a causal role in the development of cell autonomous IR in mouse and human adipocytes in a manner that is dependent on its catalytic activity.
source: Dnmt3a plays a causal role in the development of cell autonomous IR in mouse and human adipocytes in a manner that is dependent on its catalytic activity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the in vitro experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Unbiased gene expression profiling suggests that Dnmt3a acts primarily as a gene repressor.
source: In addition, unbiased gene expression profiling suggests that Dnmt3a acts as primarily as a gene repressor, and reveals a set of adipocyte-specific target genes, including Fgf21.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Dnmt3a mediates IR, at least in part, by methylating specific cis-regulatory elements in the Fgf21 gene and thus suppressing its expression.
source: Further, we demonstrate that Dnmt3a mediates IR, at least in part, by methylating specific cis-regulatory elements in the Fgf21 gene and thus suppressing its expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the MeDIP-qPCR and functional rescue experiments.

claim: DNA methylation at the FGF21 locus was elevated in human subjects with diabetes.
source: Consistent with this, Fgf21 can rescue Dnmt3a-mediated insulin resistance, and DNA methylation at the FGF21 locus was elevated in human subjects with diabetes and correlated negatively with expression of FGF21 in human adipose tissue.
evidence: This is stated based on the human adipose tissue DNA methylation analysis.

claim: DNA methylation at the FGF21 locus correlated negatively with expression of FGF21 in human adipose tissue.
source: Consistent with this, Fgf21 can rescue Dnmt3a-mediated insulin resistance, and DNA methylation at the FGF21 locus was elevated in human subjects with diabetes and correlated negatively with expression of FGF21 in human adipose tissue.
evidence: This is stated based on the correlation analysis in human adipose tissue.

claim: Fgf21 can rescue Dnmt3a-mediated insulin resistance.
source: Consistent with this, Fgf21 can rescue Dnmt3a-mediated insulin resistance, and DNA methylation at the FGF21 locus was elevated in human subjects with diabetes and correlated negatively with expression of FGF21 in human adipose tissue.
evidence: This is stated based on the recombinant FGF21 rescue experiment.

claim: Adipose Dnmt3a is a novel epigenetic mediator of insulin resistance in vitro and in vivo.
source: Taken together, our data demonstrate that adipose Dnmt3a is a novel epigenetic mediator of insulin resistance in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the abstract, summarizing all findings.
